title: The Truth Unknown to the Devotee
paragraphs: It was the wont of that Saiva adherent to invite a guest to a feast on all the important Saivite festivals.
That Saiva devotee didn’t need the assistance of any almanac to realize that it was Mahāsivarāttiri.
He wandered around looking for a guest to be fed on that day. His search proved futile. At last, he was heartened to see somebody slumbering in the choultry. He heaved a sigh of relief.

Overcome with joy, he approached him. He addressed that devotee of Lord Siva, who was dozing off with the ritual sacred ash sported on his forehead, chest and folded hands. “Sir, the one of ripeness!” he called a bit loudly.
“Who is that? I am lying here sapped of vitality due to hunger and fatigue. Why are you bothering me?” So saying the devotee got up.
The host replied, “I invite you not to appease your hunger. It is to cleanse myself of my sins. I invite you to a feast in my house.”
“Is it so? Are you offering food? Why the invitation? I don’t require one,” So saying the devotee started walking with the Saivite friend.
On the way, the guest enquired, “Is it vegetarian food or non-vegetarian?”
“How come you have such a doubt? Today is the day of Lord Siva--Sivarāttiri. God is Love. How can you forget all these and ask me such a question?”
“It is okay! In any case it is better to clear the doubt in advance. That is exactly why I enquired.”

“Okay, sir, you need not doubt at all. Dishes made of brinjal, drumstick, unripe banana and other such vegetables combined with rice of excellent quality await you. Please eat to your heart’s content.”
“Let it be so”.

“Hara Hara Siva Siva, Sambo Mahadeva! Let me squat on the veranda. Please invite me after the food gets ready.” The guest lounged on the veranda of the house muttering Siva, Siva. A few moments might have passed, when a voice assailed the ears of the guest,
Iṟaicci (meaning ‘meat’ among others)! Iṟaicci! though the explanation that followed was barely audible.
“What is this? A queer conversation is ensuing.” The guest became apprehensive.
Again the word iṟaicci loudly uttered fell on his ears.
The guest peeped inside the house.
Again the matter related to iṟaicci reared its head though the context remained unclear.
It was time for food--but the persistent sound inside was, iṟaicci, iṟaicci, iṟaicci!
The startled guest got up abruptly.
“How dare he cheats me after inviting me for a vegetarian food;” He raged, and left the place in a huff and doubled up.
What had happened actually?
The host in his anxiety to look for a devotee as a guest left his teaching of a chapter of Tolkāppiyam to his son incomplete.
Then the host was engrossed in clearing the doubts of his son.

> Iṟaicci is > The suggestive import > Paralleling the Akam thematic strand explicit. > > That from iṟaicci > There emerges an implied subtext > Beside its evocative designation of flora and fauna > Will be obvious to men of discernment.
> Designating sights of flora and fauna in nature > That are evocative of love and tenderness > Is intended to bring comfort and reassurance > To the heroine in lonesome anguish.
These are different layers of meaning of the term ‘iṟaicci’ listed in the verses 35, 36, 37 in Poruḷiyal. The father and son were discussing them.

1. ‘Iṟaicci’ refers to the suggested meaning. 2. The parallel meaning suggested is context-specific and is obvious to the learned. 3. Iṟaicci functions to privilege love in times of distress and it underlines forbearance.

(Poruḷatikāram : Poruḷiyal, verses 35, 36, 37)
